intro: cyThis step-by-step guide can help you prepare to respond to a claim for possession of a rented property.
sectionCount_one: cyEach section explains what you will be asked and any documents you may need. There is {{count}} section. Some are optional and may not apply to you.

claimantCanSeeAnswers: cyThe claimant will be able to see your answers.

content.text: cyWe will ask you to confirm your:

items: cyname
cyaddress
cydate of birth
cycontact preferences

tenancy.title: cyTenancy, occupation contract or licence agreement

content.text: cyWhen your landlord (the claimant) made their claim, they provided information about your agreement.
cyWe will ask you to confirm:

items: cyyour tenancy, occupation contract, or licence agreement and when it started
cywhether your landlord gave you notice before starting possession proceedings, and when they gave it

payments.title: cyPayments or agreements since the claim was made

content.text: cyIf the claim against you is based on rent arrears, we will ask you to confirm:

items: cyhow much money you owe
cywhether you have paid any money since the claim was made – if you have, you will be asked how much you paid and when
cywhether you have made an agreement with your landlord to repay what you owe – if you have, you will be asked how much you agreed to pay, how often you will pay and when you made this agreement

content.text: cyIf you have not made an agreement with your landlord, you can offer to pay what you owe in instalments. We will ask:

items: cyhow much you could afford to pay in addition to your current rent
cyhow often you can make this payment
cyany dependants you have (people you look after financially)
cyother adults that live in your home
cywhether you would have anywhere else to live if you were asked to leave your home
cyany personal circumstances that have led to your case that you think a judge should know about
cyany exceptional hardship you would experience if you were asked to leave your home

content.text: cyA judge can use details about your income and expenses to reach a decision on your case, and to decide how much you could afford to repay if you owe any money in rent payments.
cyIf you choose to give any details, we will ask you about:

items: cyyour regular income
cyany benefits you receive
cyif you have applied for Universal Credit
cyany priority debts
cyother regular expenses

content.text: cyWe may also ask you to upload financial documents or other supporting evidence.

disputing.title: cyDisputing other parts of the claim

content.text: cyIf any part of the claim against you is not about rent arrears, we will ask you to:

items: cyreview the claim
cytell us if you disagree with any part of it

content.text: cyYou can dispute part of the claim if you think the claimant has provided incorrect information or you disagree with what they have said. For example, you may think they did not follow the correct legal procedure, or a document they uploaded is not valid.

cyA counterclaim is a separate claim that you can make alongside your response to the claim against you. In a counterclaim, you say that the claimant owes you something. This can be money or something else.

items: cyif you want to make a counterclaim
cyto pay a fee to make a counterclaim, unless you are eligible for help with fees

support.title: cyTell us if you need support

content.text: cySome people need support to use HMCTS services.
cyYou can ask for support such as:

items: cya language interpreter
cyreasonable adjustments if you have a health condition or disability
cyspecial measures to help you feel safe at court (make sure you ask the court dealing with the case as to the special measures offered)

content.text: cyYou may also be able to choose to answer equality and diversity questions.
cyYou will be able to review all your answers and make any changes before you submit your response.
